source.title: A short project on Mamba: grokking & interpretability

record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking on an algorithmic task using a simplified Mamba-based model, extending the reported setting to a different architecture and task encoding.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes and descriptions of plots, but no numerical accuracy values or training steps. The plots themselves are not included in the supplied text. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The post trains a simplified Mamba (non-transformer) model on a mod-113 divisibility task and reports that it generalizes after overfitting. That is a new-architecture result on V1. Its gate-activation analyses track the train-test loss gap, but they identify no circuit and do not test whether the measures anticipate the jump.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that a minimal non-transformer Mamba-like model can grok, and that neuroscience tools (especially tensor decomposition of gate activations) help interpret how representations change during grokking. The summary calls the task modular addition, but it is actually binary divisibility of (x+y) by 113.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a simplified single-step Mamba-like implementation rather than the original transformer setup, and predicts a binary divisibility property of sums modulo 113 rather than reporting the original modular-addition output task.
record.method_sensitivity: The post describes analysis choices (PCA versus tensor decomposition) yielding different interpretability results; it reports no hyperparameter, optimizer, or training-set-size sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Gate activations collapse into a synchronous mode and become more specialized as grokking proceeds. The CP-decomposition epoch factors track ΔL and change direction near the extrema of ΔL's derivative; PCA trajectories showed no interpretable point.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised linear decompositions of internal activations co-vary with the train-test loss gap during grokking in non-transformer models.

fits_no_version.finding: CP-decomposition factors differ between odd-sum and even-sum inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gate-activation factors in this MinimalMambaSSM distinguish parity groups on the reported task.

record.problems: The author reports about 20 hours of work on free time using one Colab notebook. The evidence concerns one task and a simplified model; no training/test accuracy values, dataset-size comparison, controls, or uncertainty estimates are stated. The plot descriptions are qualitative.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result omitted. The text also describes token-factor salience and gate-factor specialization in the tensor decomposition, but does not connect those findings to the listed claim versions.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal LessWrong post from about 20 hours of work, covering one model and one task, with no numbers, seeds or controls. The V1 support rests only on the author's statement. Rows r2-r4 were unlinked from V2 because they track ΔL concurrently and do not identify circuits or test anticipation. The author's parity rationale (even sums are never divisible by 113) is noted but does not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not report numeric training or test accuracy, the exact delay after training accuracy saturates, or a comparison across training-set sizes.

It does not identify a generalizing circuit or memorizing components, test their removal, or identify a Fourier algorithm. It reports qualitative changes in gate activations and tensor factors over training.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm intervention is reported.

No weight-decay or low-norm intervention, critical dataset size, or ungrokking result is reported.
The study does not compare algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.

rows.subject: MinimalMambaSSM
rows.operation_detail: Trained the minimal Mamba implementation on the modular divisibility task: output whether (x+y) mod 113 equals 0.

conditions.value: binary divisibility prediction for sums modulo p=113

rows.measure: Training versus test generalization over training; the text says the model generalizes after overfitting.
rows.value: The author reports that the model exhibits grokking, described as generalizing after overfitting; no accuracy values or timing are stated.
rows.note: Qualitative report only; the text does not give the accuracy trajectory or establish the size-dependent delay.
rows.check: The author states plainly that the model groks, i.e. generalizes after overfitting. That is the effect V1 names, so the row is observed rather than partial. It is qualitative only: the plots are not in the text, and no accuracy values, timing or training-set size are given. Size-dependence of the delay is untested, not partially observed.

source_check.locator_found: Executive summary; A simple-yet-interesting enough task; A minimalistic implementation of the SSM layer; Results, opening.

rows.subject: MinimalMambaSSM
rows.operation_detail: Aggregated gate activations over tokens and examined their PCA across training epochs.

conditions.value: 2D PCA of samples by gate dimensions over epochs

rows.value: The author reports that gate activations become increasingly synchronized as learning/grokking proceeds, while gate dimensions also become more specialized.
rows.locator: Results, “A low-dimensional linear decomposition of the gating can be suggestive of learning”
rows.note: The study does not establish that these activations are a generalizing circuit or that memorizing components are removed.
rows.check: Gate activations synchronizing and specializing as grokking proceeds is a description of representation change. It does not identify a generalizing circuit or removal of memorizing components, and does not show any measure anticipating the jump. It does not measure what V2 names.

rows.subject: MinimalMambaSSM
rows.operation_detail: Compared PCA trajectories of gate activations with the train-test loss difference, ΔL=Ltest−Ltrain.
rows.measure: Whether PCA trajectories provide interpretable progress markers for grokking.
rows.value: The author reports not finding an easily interpretable point in the PCA trajectories.
rows.locator: Results, “A low-dimensional linear decomposition of the gating can be suggestive of learning”
rows.note: This is the reported outcome for the PCA analysis, before the author switched to tensor decomposition.
rows.check: The author's failure to find an interpretable point in PCA trajectories is a negative result for one analysis method. It is not evidence that a gradual mechanism is absent, so it should not be marked absent on V2.

rows.subject: MinimalMambaSSM
rows.operation_detail: Applied canonical polyadic decomposition to the gate-activation tensor and related the epochs factors to ΔL.

conditions.value: gating activations by epochs, tokens, and gate dimensions
epochs factors and extrema of ΔL

rows.measure: Temporal changes in tensor-decomposition factors relative to the train-test loss difference.
rows.value: The author reports that the epochs factors turn around near the stated maximum and minimum points of ΔL.
rows.locator: Results, “Those factors extracted with the tensor decomposition are more directly related to learning and grokking”
rows.note: The reported correspondence is qualitative; no numerical predictive performance or causal test is given.
rows.check: CP epoch factors turn near the extrema of ΔL. This is a concurrent correspondence, not a test of progress measures anticipating the jump, and no circuit or memorization component is identified.

rows.subject: MinimalMambaSSM
rows.operation_detail: Compared tensor decompositions for examples grouped by parity of the input sum.

conditions.value: canonical polyadic decomposition of gate activations

rows.value: The author reports separations between odd- and even-sum decompositions, including near coincidences and cases where one factor resembles an average of the other two.
rows.locator: Results, “Decomposing the tensor of gating activations reveals input parity”
rows.note: This finding concerns parity representation and is not directly covered by the listed claim versions.
rows.check: Parity structure in the decomposition factors is unrelated to the claim versions. The link to none is correct.
